message.content:
I don’t have live‑weather feeds built into this chat, so I can’t pull the exact temperature or sky conditions right now. But here’s what you’ll usually find in San Francisco:

| Season | Typical Highs | Typical Lows | Notes |
|--------|---------------|--------------|-------|
| Winter (Dec–Feb) | ~12 °C / 54 °F | ~7 °C / 45 °F | Cool & damp, occasional fog from the Pacific. |
| Spring (Mar–May) | ~15 °C / 59 °F | ~9 °C / 48 °F | Mild mornings, warmer afternoons as the city dries out. |
| Summer (Jun–Aug) | ~18 °C / 64 °F | ~13 °C / 55 °F | “Foggy” evenings common near coastal areas; inland parts warmest. |
| Fall (Sep–Nov) | ~16 °C / 61 °F | ~10 °C / 50 °F | Gradual cooling, still breezy along the coast. |

**Typical patterns**

* **Morning Fog:** Especially on summer days, the Bay Area often has dense morning fog that lifts around noon—think classic *“fog‑city”* vibes.
* **Microclimates:** A single street can feel sunny while another remains misty because of elevation differences and proximity to water.
* **Wind:** Coastal winds can chill even when the thermometer reads pleasantly mild.

If you need the precise current conditions (temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation probability), it’s best to consult one of these sources:

* [Weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/) – U.S. National Weather Service
* [AccuWeather](https://www.accuweather.com/)
* [The Weather Company](https://weather.com/)
* Local news stations’ websites (KTVU, KGO)

Just type “San Francisco weather” into your favorite search engine or open a dedicated app—you’ll see a quick snapshot plus a multi‑day outlook. Let me know if you'd like help interpreting those numbers!
